thesis: Held position. Microsoft reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-07-30: revenue of $90B, up 18% year over year, GAAP net income of $35.8B ($4.81 per share, +31% y/y), and adjusted EPS of $4.74 against a $4.24 consensus — a beat as reported by the sources read this run. Azure and other cloud services grew 43% in the quarter, accelerating from 40% the prior quarter, and Azure revenue passed $100B for the full fiscal year (+41%); Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats. That disclosed print, not a re-rating, is what carried the shares: the stock jumped roughly 8% after hours and the 60-day window shows +29.9%. The strongest counter-evidence is the pending securities class action in the Western District of Washington covering purchasers between 2025-05-01 and 2026-01-28, which alleges Microsoft downplayed Copilot adoption and Azure deceleration — as of the 2026-01-28 disclosure only 15 million Microsoft 365 Copilot premium customers, well below analyst estimates. That case does not change the read here, because the two facts it turns on have since reversed in the company's own disclosure: Azure growth accelerated to 43% rather than continuing to slow, and paid Copilot seats doubled to over 30 million. The suit concerns what was said about an earlier period, not the current quarter's trajectory.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerating below the low-40s percent in the next quarterly report, Copilot paid-seat growth stalling, or a scheduled court date being set in the securities class action that puts a near-term ruling in front of the position.

thesis: Held position. Dell raised its full-year fiscal 2027 AI server revenue expectation to $60B from the $50B previously guided, and at fiscal Q1 2027 (reported 2026-05-28) booked $24.4B of AI orders, recognized $16.1B of AI server revenue and closed the quarter with a $51.3B AI backlog — company-disclosed figures that explain the +15.6% 60-day move and leave the stock about 10.5% below its 52-week high. The catalyst that matters next, however, is still pending rather than confirmed: fiscal Q2 2027 results are due 2026-09-01, with management's own guidance of $44B-$45B in revenue (roughly 50% year-over-year growth at the midpoint) and consensus at $45.1B revenue and $4.91 non-GAAP EPS. The counter-case is margin rather than volume — AI server revenue converts at thinner margins than Dell's traditional infrastructure mix, so a $60B AI number does not mechanically translate into operating income — and this run's research did not surface a company-disclosed segment margin figure that settles it, so this suggests, rather than establishes, that the backlog converts profitably. That unresolved binary event one day out caps the read here regardless of how strong the backlog looks.
invalidation: Fiscal Q2 2027 revenue or EPS below management's own $44B-$45B guide, the FY27 AI server target being walked back from $60B, or AI backlog shrinking sequentially from $51.3B.
sources: Dell Technologies Q1 FY2027 press release: https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2026~05~dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results.htm

thesis: Held position, down 26.9% over the 60-day window and 40.8% below its 52-week high, so the question is whether anything disclosed has deteriorated. On the evidence read this run, it has not: Astera Labs reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $392.4M on 2026-08-04, up 27% sequentially and 104% year over year, with EPS of $0.80 against $0.64 expected, and the high-radix Scorpio X-Series entered volume production with management expecting it to become the company's largest product family in Q3. Shares nonetheless fell about 12% after that print, attributed to higher operating expenses from continued product-roadmap investment rather than to a revenue or margin miss, and the stock remains up 91.4% year to date. The read is therefore that the drawdown is a valuation de-rating in AI infrastructure names layered on an opex-driven reaction to an otherwise beating quarter — sentiment and multiple compression rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration — which is exactly the kind of explanation that leaves the counter-case open rather than answered. This run's search found no litigation or regulatory matter naming the company with a scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days, and no company-disclosed operating-margin figure that would settle whether the opex step-up is temporary.
invalidation: Scorpio X-Series failing to scale as the largest product family in Q3, a sequential revenue decline, or operating expenses continuing to outrun revenue growth in the next quarterly report.
sources: Astera Labs investor relations news releases: https://ir.asteralabs.com/news-events/news-releases

thesis: Corcept reported Q2 2026 revenue of $256.1M, up 31.7% year over year and about 21.6% ahead of estimates, and raised full-year guidance to $1.1B-$1.2B — a company-disclosed result and a company-disclosed raise, both read in sources this run, and the direct cause of the roughly 28% move that carried the shares to within 10.3% of the 52-week high on a +25.7% 60-day window. The strongest available counter-evidence is insider selling into that strength: director David Mahoney sold 103,606 shares for approximately $12.25M, cutting his holding by 8.37%. That does not change the read, because it is one director trimming a minority of a personal position, disposed of after the guidance raise rather than before it, and it stands against a forward number the company itself put on the record — the raised $1.1B-$1.2B floor is the disclosed fact, the sale is one insider's portfolio decision, and only the former binds the company. Analyst positioning is a moderate buy across eight firms (five buy, two hold, one sell), which suggests the raise is not yet a consensus view. No lawsuit, regulatory investigation, equity raise, going-concern language or executive departure surfaced in this run's research.
invalidation: Full-year guidance being cut back below $1.1B, quarterly revenue growth decelerating materially from the 31.7% year-over-year pace, or an adverse regulatory or trial outcome affecting the cortisol-modulator franchise.

thesis: Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-08-26: revenue of $96.22B against $92.07B consensus (a 4.51% beat as reported), up 105.8% year over year; Data Center revenue of $89.02B, up 117%; non-GAAP EPS of $2.22; gross margin of 75.0%; and $26B returned to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. Management guided fiscal Q3 to $108.0B, an $11.8B sequential step, and said the Vera Rubin platform is in production with purchase orders from all major customers. Those are confirmed, company-disclosed figures, and they leave the stock 6.7% below its 52-week high on a +13.3% 60-day window. The strongest counter-evidence for a long read is concentration: Data Center is roughly 92% of revenue, so the whole thesis rests on a handful of hyperscaler capex budgets, and the shares gave back part of the post-print gain in the last two sessions. That concentration does not change the read here, because the company put a specific forward number against it — a $108.0B guide that requires the sequential step to have already been ordered, plus Vera Rubin purchase orders from all major customers rather than from one — so the demand question the concentration raises is answered by disclosed orders rather than by expectation. The late-August fade coincided with a market-wide rate-shock session that hit rate-sensitive growth names generally, not with any Nvidia disclosure.
invalidation: Fiscal Q3 revenue landing below the $108.0B guide, Data Center growth decelerating sharply, gross margin falling below the low-70s, or a major hyperscaler publicly cutting AI capex plans.
sources: Yahoo Finance (Q2 FY27 earnings call highlights): https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-corp-nvda-q2-2027-050152280.html

thesis: Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-08-11 with net revenue of $1.01B against a $987.7M estimate and adjusted EPS of $3.23 against $2.97 — a beat on both lines as reported — with revenue up 109% year over year, non-GAAP gross margin of 50.4% (up 1,260 basis points), Components revenue of $649.4M (+102.7%) and Systems revenue of $356.9M (+122.6%). The company guided fiscal Q1 2027 to $1.225B-$1.275B of revenue, a 39.5%-40.5% non-GAAP operating margin and $4.05-$4.35 of non-GAAP EPS. Those disclosed figures explain the +25.6% 60-day move. The conflicting metric matters here and is not resolved: alongside the adjusted figures, one summary read this run reported a full fiscal 2026 GAAP loss per share of $92.96 against non-GAAP full-year revenue of $3.01B — a GAAP-versus-adjusted gap far too large to be ordinary stock compensation, and one this run's research could not reconcile against the company's own release. The adjusted numbers point clearly one way and that unreconciled GAAP figure points the other; until the GAAP bridge is confirmed from the filing itself, the profitability picture is unsettled even though the revenue trajectory is not.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue below the $1.225B guide, non-GAAP operating margin falling short of the 39.5% floor, or the GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridge in the 10-K confirming a structural rather than one-off loss.
sources: Lumentum Q4 FY2026 press release (SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026055726/lite_ex991xq4fy26.htm

thesis: Coherent reported fiscal Q4 2026 in August with quarterly sales of $2,045.5M (up 34% year over year), full-year revenue of $7,118.2M, a return to profitability and EPS of $1.74 against $1.58 expected — a beat as reported — and in the same month began sampling 300mm high-thermal-conductivity silicon carbide substrates to major AI semiconductor customers for datacenter thermal management. Against that, the stock is down 16.7% over the 60-day window and sits 36.7% below its 52-week high, including a 14.23% single-session drop on 2026-08-10 that sources attribute to investors de-risking AI optics names after a large run and on a rich valuation, plus an optics-versus-memory allocation debate — sentiment and positioning rather than a disclosed deterioration. That is the read and also its weakness: when the explanation for a large drawdown is that holders rotated out rather than that anything in the disclosures got worse, nothing in the sourced facts tells you when that rotation stops, so the counter-case is engaged but unsettled.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue or margin guidance below the fiscal Q4 run rate, the return to profitability reversing, or datacenter/AI optics orders slowing in the next report.

thesis: Marvell reported fiscal Q2 results on 2026-08-28 with revenue up 37% to $2.7B, $39M above its own May guidance, and raised its fiscal 2028 outlook to roughly $18B (about 50% year-over-year growth) from $16.5B. Shares nonetheless fell 6% because that raised outlook fell short of elevated expectations after a commercial agreement disclosed 2026-08-19 gave Google the right to buy up to 58,970,907 Marvell shares at $206.58, roughly $12.18B at the strike. That warrant is the reason for the flag on this name: it is a pending equity issuance of about 59 million shares disclosed within the last 90 days, and while it is consideration in a customer relationship rather than a capital raise, the dilution is real if Google exercises. The disclosed operating facts are positive — a revenue beat against the company's own guide and a raised multi-year target — but they arrive alongside a share-issuance right and an outlook the market judged insufficient, so the evidence offsets rather than resolving into a clean read.
invalidation: Fiscal 2028 revenue guidance being cut back toward $16.5B, the Google agreement not translating into disclosed design wins or revenue, or data-center revenue growth decelerating below the 37% pace.

thesis: SanDisk is down 10.2% over the 60-day window while remaining up sharply on the year, and the sourced explanation for the pullback is a macro rate shock — a 2.2% fall on 2026-08-28 attributed to Fed commentary hitting the recently spun-off NAND maker — rather than any company disclosure. The operating backdrop read this run points the other way: AI infrastructure demand is described as driving tight NAND supply and rising pricing, recent supply agreements carry a floor price of roughly $0.29 per gigabyte broadly in line with Q2 2026 average selling prices, and the company has initiated a $14 billion buyback. Mizuho trimmed its price target to $1,875 from $1,900 on 2026-08-24, a marginal change rather than a thesis reversal. This thesis must be read with an explicit caveat: the sources available this run reported mutually inconsistent share prices for the same date (one gave $23.18, another $1,484.98 against the $1,549.88 snapshot taken from the broker), so no company-disclosed quarterly revenue or EPS figure could be confirmed here, and none is asserted. The pricing and buyback facts are second-hand and the print is unconfirmed.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing rolling over below the disclosed ~$0.29/GB floor, the buyback being suspended, or a quarterly report showing average selling prices or bit shipments declining sequentially.

thesis: Rocket Lab is down 36.4% over the 60-day window and 57.6% below its 52-week high, and the sourced explanation is mostly not company-specific: the stock fell 36.1% in July with, as one source puts it, little negative business-specific news, caught in a broad valuation pullback across space names — SpaceX fell roughly 36.6% over the same July stretch — against a flat S&P 500 and a Nasdaq down 3.2%. The company's own August disclosures were largely good: record Q2 revenue of $234.07M (+62% year over year), a record $2.36B backlog and a $397M U.S. Space Force Flatellites contract. Two company-specific negatives sit alongside them: a loss of $0.08 per share against $0.06 expected, and management declining to reaffirm a first Neutron flight before year-end while still guiding Stage 1 tank production toward delivering the rocket to the launchpad in Q4 2026 — the shares fell more than 7% after hours on that combination. Even after the decline the stock trades at more than 70 times trailing sales while unprofitable. The bull case is the backlog and contract flow; the bear case is that the single catalyst underwriting the multiple has an unreaffirmed date, and this run's research cannot settle which resolves first, so the sector-driven drawdown is not by itself a reason to buy.
invalidation: Neutron's first flight being formally slipped out of 2026 or the Q4 launchpad delivery target being missed would confirm the avoid; a reaffirmed flight date with a successful first launch, or backlog conversion into positive operating cash flow, would overturn it.

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is down 30.6% over the 60-day window and 55.9% below its 52-week high. The sourced driver of the sharpest leg — a 15.5% fall on 2026-08-28 while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were up 1.1% and 1.8% on the week — is macro rather than company-specific: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled inflation is the Fed's focus, raising the odds of a rate hike, and AST is building its satellite constellation largely on borrowed money, so its funding cost and the arithmetic of those investments move directly with rates. Earlier in August the stock fell on SpaceX changing its launch operations, since AST depends on third-party rockets. The disclosed fundamentals are genuinely two-sided: Q2 revenue of $31.5M against $1.2M a year earlier is real commercial traction, but the net loss widened to $230.9M in the same quarter. A capital-intensive pre-scale operator whose losses are widening faster than its revenue is growing, whose launch access sits with a third party, and whose valuation is being repriced by rate expectations, is not a setup this run can resolve into a clear net read.
invalidation: A sustained fall in rate-hike expectations plus a quarter showing the net loss narrowing rather than widening, or a secured multi-launch agreement removing the third-party launch dependency, would overturn the avoid.

thesis: Intel is down 25.6% over the 60-day window on two disclosed, company-specific events. First, an upsized public equity offering of about 210.5 million shares priced at $95, raising roughly $20B — increased from $15B — at about a 6.5% discount to the prior close, leaving a supply overhang the sources cite directly as pressuring the shares. Second, Intel Foundry Services posted a $2.8B operating loss in Q2 2026, with one source projecting more than $10B of cumulative foundry operating losses through the end of 2027 before the business approaches the scale needed for profitability. Alongside these, CPU market share is described as hitting a three-decade low while AMD EPYC takes 34% server share. The plausible positive is that the $20B raise is precisely what funds the foundry build-out to that scale, and that a capitalized balance sheet plus reported strategic investment interest de-risks the turnaround. This run cannot settle that against the dilution: the raise is confirmed and immediate, the foundry profitability it buys is years out and unquantified in any company-disclosed target found here.
invalidation: Foundry operating losses narrowing materially from the $2.8B quarterly rate, or external foundry customer commitments being disclosed at scale, would overturn the avoid; continued share loss in server and client CPUs would confirm it.

thesis: Corning is down 24.4% over the 60-day window and 45.2% below its 52-week high, and the drivers read this run are several rather than one. The Q2 report on 2026-07-28 beat Wall Street estimates on both revenue and earnings, but third-quarter guidance came in slightly below an elevated consensus and triggered a single-day decline of more than 20%. Within that quarter, Optical Communications — the AI-driven growth segment underwriting the multiple — grew 32% year over year to $2.07B, decelerating from 36% the prior quarter. Separately, reports that Apple scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone knocked the shares 2.7% and removed an expected specialty-glass program. Broader AI-sector rotation, profit-taking from all-time highs and softer smartphone demand for Gorilla Glass are cited on top. A beat paired with light guidance, decelerating growth in the segment that matters most, and a cancelled customer program is a mixed picture that does not resolve into a net read, and none of the individual factors is dominant enough to make the drawdown an entry.
invalidation: Optical Communications growth reaccelerating above the 36% prior-quarter pace, or Q3 results landing above the guidance that caused the de-rating, would overturn the avoid; further deceleration or additional customer program losses would confirm it.

thesis: SpaceX is down 11.3% over the 60-day window, and the dominant driver in the sources read this run is mechanical share supply rather than operations: around 319 million shares held by early employees and investors became eligible to trade as part of a staggered lockup that will release roughly 88% of the company's 13 billion shares through 2027, and the stock fell back below its $135 IPO price on that unlock plus competing-rocket headlines. The Q2 report on 2026-08-04 was genuinely two-sided — revenue jumped 92% from $4.1B a year earlier and the net loss narrowed to $541M from $1B, but capital expenditure rose more than sixfold year over year to $18.37B, of which $15.83B went to AI, against a $13.22B average analyst estimate, and the shares fell about 8% after hours on that spend. Improving revenue and a narrowing loss set against a capex figure that overshot expectations by roughly $5B, with a known multi-year supply overhang still to come, is an offsetting picture and a poor moment to establish a position.
invalidation: Capital expenditure moderating toward prior guidance while revenue growth holds, and the remaining lockup tranches clearing without sustained price pressure, would overturn the avoid; further capex escalation with a widening loss would confirm it.

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics is down 11% over the 60-day window and 53.9% below its 52-week high, and the proximate cause is a disclosed financing rather than a demand problem. On 2026-08-21 the company entered an Equity Distribution Agreement with Raymond James for a $600M at-the-market offering; the stock fell about 10% after hours on that announcement and roughly 12.3% pre-market the following Monday, extending a 3.32% decline. The operating results point the other way: record Q2 revenue of $191.9M on AI and CATV demand, non-GAAP profitability achieved, Q3 revenue guided up to $290M, and sources describing capacity — not demand — as the binding constraint, with a major U.S. manufacturing expansion under way. That is the plausible positive, and it is exactly why the raise exists: the expansion has to be funded. But an ATM program of that size against a company this size is open-ended dilution priced into every rally until it is drawn down, and this run cannot establish how quickly the funded capacity converts to the guided revenue, so the two sides do not resolve.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing at or above the $290M guide with the ATM largely undrawn would overturn the avoid; the program being drawn aggressively, or capacity expansion slipping while guidance is cut, would confirm it.
sources: Applied Optoelectronics investor relations news releases: https://investors.ao-inc.com/news-events/press-releases

thesis: Cerebras reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-12 and the two headline revenue figures point in opposite directions, so both belong here: GAAP revenue of $180M missed the $194M expected, while the company-preferred core revenue figure — which strips out pass-through revenue and amortization of customer warrant assets — was $210M. On the bottom line the adjusted loss of $0.05 per share was better than the $0.17 expected, but the GAAP net loss was $450.5M, of which $386.6M was stock compensation. The stock fell about 14% after hours on that print and now sits 52% below its 52-week high, only 14.5% above its 52-week low, on a -10.1% 60-day window. The offsetting positives are real: full-year guidance was raised, core gross margin was guided to 38%-40% for the current quarter, the CS-4 system launched in late August, and ARK Invest bought $8.84M of stock on 2026-08-18. A quarter where the GAAP top line misses while the adjusted top line beats, and where the loss is dominated by a stock-compensation charge nearly matching quarterly core revenue, is unresolved evidence, not an entry.
invalidation: GAAP revenue meeting or beating consensus in the next quarter with stock compensation falling as a share of revenue, and core gross margin landing in the guided 38%-40% band, would overturn the avoid; another GAAP revenue miss or a break below the 52-week low would confirm it.
